calls.title: GrowthBook and Felt
calls.summary: Felt's meeting focused on transitioning from Statsig to GrowthBook driven by dissatisfaction with Statsig's degraded quality and support. Matt Menzi highlighted performance issues, bugs, and dashboard shortcomings at Statsig, pushing for a more reliable option like GrowthBook. Dan Wathne praised GrowthBook's open-source model, emphasizing community support and scalability, critical for Felt’s data demands. GrowthBook offers warehouse-native solutions, enabling Felt to handle complex queries efficiently. The platform's experimentation capabilities, including feature flagging and streamlined migration from Statsig, align with Felt’s operational needs. A focus on security compliance, necessary for Felt's health tech context, and continuous product enhancements further solidified GrowthBook as a favorable choice.
calls.keywords: experiment platform, data warehouse, migration, AB testing, feature flags, HIPAA compliance

calls.title: Growthbook <> Felt - Demo/Pricing Sync
calls.summary: Participants discussed the development of GrowthBook’s analytics features, including integration with Slack for event notifications and status updates, though current limitations in dashboard embedding were noted. Dashboard sharing options are being enhanced for external client access, with permissioned sharing similar to Google Docs and plans for improved export options. Logan highlighted the complexity of access control for different user roles, while future analytics capabilities such as cohort analysis and funnel tracking are set to launch in the coming months, reflecting a commitment to enhancing features to meet client needs. Discussions on pricing strategies acknowledged client budget constraints and the necessity of flexible trial arrangements to facilitate onboarding.
calls.keywords: analytics, dashboarding, Slack integration, event forwarding, pricing negotiation, BAA compliance
